## Motivation

Editors screening peer-reviewer candidates usually check for direct
co-authorship with a manuscript's authors and stop there. In a small
field, that misses two common conflict patterns: a candidate who
shares a *frequent collaborator* with an author (second-degree
conflict), and a candidate who shares *federal funding* with an author
with no joint publication yet. `coiCheckR` checks all three and
returns evidence for each -- not a conflicted/clear verdict, since
that judgment call should stay with the editor.

This vignette's example is a real, consented ground-truth case rather
than fictional names: `"Ravi Janani"` and `"Ghosh A"` as two reviewer
candidates, being screened against a manuscript by `"Brenner E"` and
`"Krishnan A"`. Ravi Janani has a known direct co-authorship with
Brenner E, *and* both a co-authorship and shared NIH funding with
Krishnan A -- two independent evidence types for the same pair. Ghosh
A's actual relationship to the manuscript's authors, if any, is left
for the live output below to show.

A full forename (`"Ravi Janani"` rather than `"Ravi J"`) both searches
PubMed more precisely for a common surname and is handled correctly
for matching -- see `vignette("testing-workflow")` for exactly how.
`affiliation` narrows further still; list every institution across a
multi-institution career as a separate vector element (OR-combined),
since each only matches the affiliation recorded *on that specific
publication* -- and prefer a short, distinctive word per institution
(`"Virginia"`) over its full or colloquial name (`"Virginia Tech"`
literally returns zero hits here, since PubMed matches a multi-word
element as a phrase, not word-by-word, and that exact phrase never
appears in any affiliation string on record).


``` r
library(coiCheckR)
```

## A single candidate, all three checks


``` r
report <- checkCoi(
  candidate_name = "Ravi Janani",
  author_names = "Brenner E",
  affiliation = c("Colorado", "Michigan", "Rutgers", "Virginia"),
  check_second_degree = TRUE,
  check_funding = TRUE
)
report
#> COI screen: Ravi Janani vs. 1 author(s)
#>   status:                  potential_conflict
#>   direct co-authorship:    8 hit(s)
#>   second-degree overlap:   28 hit(s)
#>   shared NIH awards:       0 hit(s)
#> 
#>   -- direct --
#> # A tibble: 8 × 4
#>   candidate   author     PMID      year
#>   <chr>       <chr>      <chr>    <int>
#> 1 Ravi Janani Brenner EP 38809013  2024
#> 2 Ravi Janani Brenner EP 40425396  2025
#> 3 Ravi Janani Brenner EP 41040319  2025
#> 4 Ravi Janani Brenner EP 41279520  2025
#> 5 Ravi Janani Brenner EP 41641989  2026
#> 6 Ravi Janani Brenner EP 41935917  2026
#> 7 Ravi Janani Brenner E  42079283  2026
#> 8 Ravi Janani Brenner EP 42523430  2026
#> 
#>   -- second-degree (review, not auto-exclude) --
#> # A tibble: 28 × 4
#>    candidate_collaborator linked_author n_shared_with_candidate evidence_PMID
#>    <chr>                  <chr>                           <int> <chr>        
#>  1 Anantharaman V         Brenner E                           2 38809013     
#>  2 Aravind L              Brenner E                           2 38809013     
#>  3 Boyer EA               Brenner E                           2 41279520     
#>  4 Boyer EA               Brenner E                           2 42523430     
#>  5 Burke JT               Brenner E                           3 41279520     
#>  6 Clatworthy AE          Brenner E                           2 41040319     
#>  7 Clatworthy AE          Brenner E                           2 41641989     
#>  8 Cosimi LA              Brenner E                           2 41040319     
#>  9 Cosimi LA              Brenner E                           2 41641989     
#> 10 Datta P                Brenner E                           3 38809013     
#> # ℹ 18 more rows
```

`report$direct` holds one row per shared publication (PMID and year),
`report$second_degree` one row per collaborator-mediated path, and
`report$funding` one row per shared NIH award -- each independently
verifiable evidence, not a verdict. `report$status` and
`report$sources_failed` (see `?checkCoi`) tell you whether that's a
genuine clean result or one where a source didn't respond.

## Screening a shortlist at once


``` r
batch <- checkCoiBatch(
  candidate_names = c("Ravi Janani", "Ghosh A"),
  author_names = "Krishnan A",
  check_second_degree = TRUE,
  check_funding = TRUE
)

batch$summary
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   candidate   status           n_direct n_second_degree n_funding sources_failed
#>   <chr>       <chr>               <int>           <int>     <int> <chr>         
#> 1 Ravi Janani potential_confl…        0               0         1 ""            
#> 2 Ghosh A     no_conflict_det…        0               0         0 ""
```

`formatCoiSummary()` turns the same result into plain-text lines
suitable for pasting into an email to a co-editor:


``` r
cat(formatCoiSummary(batch), sep = "\n")
#> Ravi Janani -- 0 direct, 0 second-degree, 1 funding [potential_conflict]
#> Ghosh A -- 0 direct, 0 second-degree, 0 funding [no_conflict_detected]
```

## Shared NIH funding

Some conflicts show up in funding before they show up in the
literature -- e.g. a shared multi-PI award with no joint publication
yet. `reporterSharedAwards()` cross-references NIH RePORTER project
numbers directly:


``` r
this_year <- as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y"))
last_10y <- (this_year - 9):this_year

reporterSharedAwards("Ravi, Janani", "Krishnan, Arjun", fiscal_years = last_10y)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 12
#>   project_num    fiscal_year_candidate org_name_candidate project_title_candid…¹
#>   <chr>                          <int> <chr>              <chr>                 
#> 1 5R21AI169301-…                  2023 <NA>               Mechanism-guided drug…
#> # ℹ abbreviated name: ¹​project_title_candidate
#> # ℹ 8 more variables: contact_PI_candidate <chr>, all_PIs_candidate <list>,
#> #   fiscal_year_author <int>, org_name_author <chr>,
#> #   project_title_author <chr>, contact_PI_author <chr>, all_PIs_author <list>,
#> #   queried_author <chr>
```

## Visualizing a batch result


``` r
reports <- batch[setdiff(names(batch), "summary")]
plotCoiNetwork(reports)
```

![plot of chunk plot](coiCheckR_files/figure-precompiled/plot-1.png)

## A note on evidence vs. verdicts

Every function in this package returns evidence -- PMIDs, award
numbers, collaborator names -- rather than a binary conflicted/clear
flag. Two candidates with the same number of `direct` hits can warrant
different editorial decisions depending on recency, the nature of the
collaboration, and context the tool has no way to know. `coiCheckR` is
meant to make that judgment call easier to make well, not to make it
for you.

For a lower-level, function-by-function walkthrough (useful when
verifying the package's own plumbing rather than just using it), see
`vignette("testing-workflow")`.
